sectors.ai: Buy YELO and ELIT on momentum, but rotate into INET and AREA for sustained earnings visibility as US tech weakness filters through. Trim EPAC and PMUI into strength—their gains lack volume confirmation. Keep net exposure neutral; the ID/US divergence signals local liquidity support, not a fundamental re-rating. Add on any pullback to 5-day moving averages.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Coal equities are re-rating on resilient thermal demand and tight Indonesian supply, favoring low-cost producers like ADRO and MBAP with export flexibility.
Nickel and downstream processing names (INPS, AADI) benefit from EV battery demand and government-backed smelter expansions, despite global price volatility.
Energy service and infrastructure plays (SLB, BAJA) are gaining from upstream capex recovery, but gains are selective and require earnings delivery to sustain.
sectors.ai: Buy MBAP on its 24.8% surge, but treat as momentum—lock partial profits and trail stops; rotate into ADRO for coal cash-flow resilience and INPS for nickel upside. Sector breadth is positive but not euphoric, so add on dips rather than chase. Trim ALKA and BAJA into strength, as their moves lack volume confirmation.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's 2030 renewable mix target and new presidential regulation on solar-plus-storage PPAs are structurally lifting domestic project pipelines for KEEN, LAPD, and ESSA.
Falling global solar module and battery costs are improving IRR for Indonesian IPPs, making climate-tech names like POWR and HGII more competitive against coal.
US policy uncertainty and rate swings will keep pressuring US-exposed renewables, but Indonesia's domestic demand and local content rules insulate high-ID-revenue players, favoring AWK and PKPK.
sectors.ai: Buy dips in KEEN, LAPD, and ESSA on Indonesia's accelerating renewable mandate, but cap exposure given US-driven volatility. Prioritize names with domestic revenue and PPAs; avoid US-linked laggards. Expect rotation into climate-tech as government pushes 2030 solar and storage targets—accumulate POWR and HGII on pullbacks.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rupiah stability and falling inflation are boosting domestic purchasing power, sustaining FMCG volume growth despite global commodity volatility.
Premiumization and halal-certified product launches are driving margin expansion for mid-cap consumer names, especially in snacks and personal care.
E-commerce and direct-to-consumer channels are accelerating distribution reach beyond Java, unlocking new demand in tier-2/3 cities for fast-moving goods.
sectors.ai: Buy selective momentum names (SRSN, KICI, OILS) on strong volume, but rotate profits into defensive staples (UNVR, ICBP) as the rally looks overheated; expect consolidation within 2-3 weeks, so trim laggards and hold cash for pullback entries.

sectors.name: Infrastructure

Conglomerate infrastructure plays (BNBR, AKPI) are gaining on asset-recycling and divestment catalysts, but sustainability hinges on execution discipline.

Rotate into contractors (KRYA, ASLI) on Jokowi's final-year project acceleration, but trim BNBR on speculative froth. Hold PIPA for gas distribution monopoly leverage.

sectors.name: Logistics
themes: Indonesia's e-commerce and manufacturing export volumes are structurally rising, driving sustained demand for third-party logistics and freight forwarding services.
Port infrastructure bottlenecks and rising fuel costs are creating pricing power for domestic trucking and shipping operators, supporting margin expansion.
Government push for downstream processing and new industrial parks in Eastern Indonesia is shifting cargo flows, benefiting regional logistics players with last-mile networks.
sectors.ai: Accumulate logistics names on IDX strength, led by PPGL and SOCI, as domestic volume growth and port congestion sustain pricing power; US weakness is a headwind but not a trigger. Add on pullbacks toward support, targeting TRUK and BULL for mid-cap torque, while NELY offers defensive yield. Trim SAFE if it fails to hold gains above 3.5%.

sectors.name: Crypto & Digital Assets
themes: Indonesia's pending crypto tax framework is accelerating demand for privacy coins and DEXs, as traders seek to minimize on-chain traceability ahead of stricter reporting rules.
Layer-2 scaling solutions like MNT are gaining structural traction as domestic fintech firms integrate cheaper settlement rails for remittances and micro-payments.
Global regulatory divergence—US ETF approvals vs. ASEAN tightening—is widening liquidity pools toward permissionless assets, favoring UNI and CAKE as durable yield-bearing proxies.
sectors.ai: Rotate into privacy and DEX-native tokens (XMR, UNI, CAKE) as regulatory noise in Indonesia favors decentralized rails over exchange-linked assets; MNT's +10% signals layer-2 momentum that aligns with Jakarta's digital-economy push. Take profits on DASH and LIT into strength, and add MORPHO on dips for leveraged-lending exposure.
